# Discussion and conclusion {background-color="#491106ff"}

## Discussion and conclusion

:::: {.incremental style="font-size: 120%;"}

- Findings: perceiving merit and endorsing privilege raise MJP; perceiving privilege lowers it
- Part of a broader agenda on the policy feedback of commodification [@lindh_public_2015; @busemeyer_welfare_2020; @koos_moral_2019]; two prior longitudinal studies of ours, but not multidimensional [@castillo_perceptions_2025; @castillo_justification_2026]
- Contribution: multidimensional measurement plus SEM disentangles distinct paths, net of measurement error [@meuleman_welfare_2020]
- Limits: cross-sectional, one country; next: social structure (class, stratification, context), conjoint experiments, cross-country

::::


::: {.notes}

To conclude, a few points.

First, we have shown that it is not enough to talk about meritocracy in general. Its dimensions matter and do not work the same way: perceiving merit and accepting privilege raise support for market-based welfare, while perceiving privilege lowers it.

Second, this work seeks to contribute to the welfare attitudes literature, particularly to the literature on the policy feedback effects of commodification, by positioning meritocratic beliefs as a key driver of preferences for market-based welfare. Our team has been pushing this link across a couple of publications, and we now extend it by measuring meritocracy in multiple dimensions.

Third, we also want to contribute on the methodological side. Modeling these beliefs as latent factors in an SEM separates measurement error from structure and recovers distinct paths that a summative index would obscure, an approach that is transferable to other beliefs and domains.

Finally, this work is cross-sectional and single-country. From here, our aim is more sociological: to embed these beliefs in social structure and examine how class, stratification, and context shape these relationships. In parallel, we are building conjoint experiments and cross-country comparisons. Thank you.


:::
